The point $P(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\frac{1}{2})$ lies on the unit circle, as shown. What is $\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ?$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14222207/assets/1ffb0a83abf7e736c47035f4f337c36a6bb129fd0d64fe0ac3bfe8e46c194a11.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $x=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $y=\frac{1}{2}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Knowing that $\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta },$ we can calculate $\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta :$

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta =\frac{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})}{(\frac{1}{2})}=\sqrt{3}.
$$
